newsitem.title: USA: CSX, Norfolk Southern close Conrail tender.
newsitem.headline: CSX, Norfolk Southern close Conrail tender.

text.p: CSX Corp. and Norfolk Southern Corp. said Tuesday they have closed their joint tender offer for Conrail Inc., moving the $10.3 billion railroad deal closer to completion.
They said 57.4 million Conrail shares have been tendered, which together with what the two companies currently own, represents 96 percent of the outstanding Conrail shares.
They said they have accepted for payment more than 94 percent of the oustanding Conrail shares not already owned by the two companies.
After a months-long bidding war, CSX and Norfolk Southern agreed in early April to the $115-a-share joint offer for Conrail.
Norfolk Southern is paying $5.9 billion for 58 percent of Conrail and CSX paying $4.3 billion for the remaining 42 percent.
Conrail shares not bought in the tender will be converted into the right to receive $115 cash per share in the merger.

Norfolk Southern Chairman, President and Chief Executive Daviod Goode said that with the financing part of the deal nearly completed, the two bidders will submit to the Surface Transportation Board in mid-June their plan to improve the rail system in the East.
CSX's stock fell 37.5 cents to $52.625, Conrail was unchanged at $114.75 and Norfolk Southern slipped 87.5 cents to $95.875 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
